rejected.description: Feathers down, lances level, the hill becomes a fall. In July–September 1683, Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha’s army ringed Vienna. A coalition under King Jan III Sobieski crossed the Danube and, on September 12, rolled off the Kahlenberg in one of history’s largest coordinated cavalry charges. The Ottoman lines buckled; the siege collapsed before nightfall. This is what it looked like: a sea of tents and trenches tilting up into the visor, drums booming from pavilions, matchlock smoke swallowing color, stakes and guy-ropes snapping under hooves as brass, silk, and dust flashed past in shuddering bursts. By dawn the siege was memory, the camp overrun, and the road into Central Europe swung away from Ottoman hands. Kara Mustafa paid with his life that winter; new Holy League campaigns pushed the frontier back for a generation. Told from the enemy’s saddle at the #BattleOfVienna under #JanIIISobieski against #KaraMustafa in #1683, this slice of #MilitaryHistory rides the charge that broke the ring.
